candidates.title: США вже тиждень не пояснюють обмеження Starshield над окупованими територіями України
candidates.summary: Обмеження швидкості роботи супутникової системи Starshield над тимчасово окупованими територіями України діють уже сьомий день поспіль, однак ані Міністерство оборони США, ані компанія SpaceX досі не пояснили причин їх запровадження. Про це заявив тимчасовий повірений у справах України у Сполучених
candidates.full: Обмеження швидкості роботи супутникової системи Starshield над тимчасово окупованими територіями України діють уже сьомий день поспіль, однак ані Міністерство оборони США, ані компанія SpaceX досі не пояснили причин їх запровадження. Про це заявив тимчасовий повірений у справах України у Сполучених Штатах Денис Сеник у соцмережі X. За словами дипломата, українське посольство продовжує отримувати звернення від американських журналістів, які намагаються з’ясувати причини обмежень. Денис Сеник повідомив, що американські медіа отримують від Пентагону відповіді про нібито відсутність будь-яких обмежень у роботі Starshield. Водночас дипломат наголосив, що такі заяви суперечать ситуації, яку фіксують українські військові. «Хочу заявити однозначно: це суперечить тому, що відбувається на місцях. Я можу підтвердити, що обмеження швидкості справді діють», — написав Сеник. За його словами, проблема має безпосередні оперативні наслідки для України та потребує термінового вирішення. «Ці обмеження мають реальні оперативні наслідки для України та потребують термінового пояснення й вирішення. Сім днів без відповідей — це на сім днів забагато», — наголосив дипломат. За повідомленнями про ситуацію на фронті, протягом останнього тижня українські військові фіксують обмеження роботи супутникового зв’язку Starshield поблизу лінії бойового зіткнення та над тимчасово окупованими територіями. Йдеться про швидкісний поріг приблизно 161 км/год, або 100 миль на годину. За наявною інформацією, після перевищення цієї швидкості можуть виникати проблеми зі стабільністю супутникового з’єднання. Такі обмеження ускладнюють застосування українських безпілотників-перехоплювачів, які використовують супутниковий зв’язок для керування та передачі даних. Особливо це стосується протидії швидкісним російським ударним дронам, зокрема реактивним модифікаціям «Шахедів». Водночас технічні причини обмежень і можливість їх усунення наразі офіційно не пояснені. Раніше президент України Володимир Зеленський заявив, що обмеження Starshield ускладнюють перехоплення російських ударних безпілотників. За словами глави держави, значна частина успішних російських ударів «Шахедами» по українських підстанціях пов’язана саме з обмеженнями швидкості роботи супутникових терміналів. Президент наголошував, що такі технічні обмеження негативно впливають на можливості України захищати енергетичну інфраструктуру від повітряних атак. Читайте також: Обмеження швидкості Starlink впливає на роботу української ППО — Ігнат Зазначимо, що 105 членів двопартійної групи підтримки України в Палаті представників Конгресу США закликали відновити українським військовим повний доступ до Starshield. Відповідну вимогу вони адресували адміністрації президента США Дональда Трампа та компанії SpaceX. Американські законодавці звернули увагу на вплив обмежень супутникового зв’язку на оборонні можливості України.

candidates.title: The United States Has Space Weapons: How Should It Use Them?
candidates.summary: The idea of warfare in space has been present at least since the first Gulf War was declared the “first space war,” but the potential for armed conflict in the space domain has been growing for over a decade in both urgency and public consciousness. The inception of the U.S. Space Force brought with
candidates.full: The idea of warfare in space has been present at least since the first Gulf War was declared the “first space war,” but the potential for armed conflict in the space domain has been growing for over a decade in both urgency and public consciousness. The inception of the U.S. Space Force brought with it open discussion of space as a warfighting domain, and Russia’s aggression in Ukraine brought with it explicit discussion of potentially targeting commercial satellites on orbit. In this context, Secretary of the Air Force Troy Meink recently announced that, for the first time, “the Space Force now has on-orbit space control weapons capable of defending the joint force against hostile adversary action.” One initial question with this announcement may be whether such weapons are legal. They are, as comprehensively discussed here. This leaves us not just to consider what would be lawful targets for counter-space weapons in an armed conflict, but also what the United States, as a whole, wants the answer to be. A particular consideration is the legitimacy of commercial satellites as potential targets. A starting point to answering these questions is the legal framework already in place. However, the law only provides a floor, or minimum requirement. It is a baseline, and the law of armed conflict–albeit with some clear red lines–contains fairly permissive rules that are focused on process for competent decision authorities (often commanders, but in the highly strategic context of space, more often senior policymakers and civilian leaders) rather than a specific outcome in a particular targeting scenario. Moreover, there are no space-specific laws for targeting; instead, rules for space are derived from general practice and rules that transcend the domains of conflict (that is, laws that apply to land, air, sea, cyber, and space generally), with domain-specific nuance either coming from explicit domain-specific agreements or the factual application of the unique aspects of the domain to the broader law. Given this, the United States has an opportunity to shape the development and understanding of the norms, rules, and law related to what does, and does not, constitute a legitimate military objective in space. It is important to remember that the military objective test is only one part of a targeting decision, along with a proportionality and precautions analysis, any rules of engagement, or other policy requirements; but it is a foundational, essential part of the analysis and one the United States should not take lightly as it considers what is both responsible and reasonably workable behavior in the space domain. Targeting and the Law of Armed Conflict So, under the law of armed conflict, what is a legitimate target (that is, a lawful military objective)? Fortunately, there is great consensus on this matter—or at least on the legal test—among parties to Additional Protocol I of the Geneva Conventions (the vast majority of states, including China and Russia, but not including the United States), the United States under the DoD Law of War Manual (section 5.6.3), and the International Committee of the Red Cross’s widely-accepted assertion of customary international law: “military objectives are limited to those objects which by their nature, location, purpose or use make an effective contribution to military action and whose total or partial destruction, capture or neutralization, in the circumstances ruling at the time, offers a definite military advantage.” To satisfy this two-part test, an attacker must determine that a space object makes an “effective contribution” to the adversary, and that its elimination offers the attacker a “definite military advantage.” This is fairly broad and lays out a process for the first step in a targeting decision (with additional rules such as those on proportionality and taking precautions in attack following only if this threshold test is satisfied), relying on the good faith judgement and factual assessment of an attacker. Military satellites for all warfighting purposes like Space Force- (or other Defense organization-) procured, operated, and controlled craft would clearly be military objectives (and under the DoD Law of War Manual section 5.6.4, they are “categorically recognized” as military objectives such that the test need not even be applied). Most commercial capabilities and systems could pass the test as well. By its assertions, Russia has suggested that Starlink, as used by Ukraine in its national defense, would qualify. Similarly, recent reports of Chinese commercial imagery being used by Iran for targeting U.S. bases suggest that such commercial satellites, by their use, made an effective contribution to the Iranian war effort; if the elimination of that satellite or capability would have adversely impacted Iran’s ability to effectively strike U.S. positions, there is a strong argument that their neutralization would offer a definite military advantage under the circumstances ruling at the time. The Space Force is structured to incorporate civilian and commercial capabilities into its warfighting architecture under its Commercial Space Strategy, including during war. The Space Force’s Commercial Augmentation Space Reserve concept is specifically designed for commercial firms to be “called upon in wartime to surge delivery of satellite-derived capabilities,” and has conducted its own wargame events. Even if limited to support functions, those functions are essential and indispensable to the warfighter, as the new Chief of Space Operations (CSO), General Douglas Schiess, recently noted related to Operation Epic Fury. But this does not mean all commercial satellites supporting U.S. operations are automatically legitimate targets; the military objective analysis is complex and nuanced, and warfighting staffs consider a range of factors in the analysis—and may come to differing conclusions. Consider, for example, the Space Force’s Joint Commercial Operations Cell (JCO), which purports to integrate data and services from a loose conglomeration of commercial providers to execute or enhance military missions, such as Space Domain Awareness (SDA) and Tactical Surveillance, Reconnaissance, and Tracking (TacSRT), including support to “all-domain combat operations.” On its face, it appears that its commercial participants could be lawful targets. But, is it so disaggregated (with each participant providing only a negligible role, moderated through this cell) that no one participating commercial object actually makes an effective contribution? Similarly, Starlink is not one satellite but a constellation of over 11,000 that collectively deliver its mesh capability, and with significant redundancy. Would destroying one (or some—and how many) satellite(s) offer a definite military advantage under the circumstances ruling at the time? Some have concluded that, at least at 2,000 satellites, Starlink would be a valid military objective (notwithstanding proportionality and precautions challenges), but does the five-fold increase mean the effects would be de minimus or too indefinite or attenuated to form such an advantage; is this a universal view; and, who decides? As it stands, these determinations are in the hands of the targeting state. In terrestrial campaigns, the United States attacks networks and target systems. For instance, in the counter-ISIS effort, innumerable individuals, small weapons caches, and makeshift headquarters buildings were prosecuted piecemeal, removing perhaps only one or two fighters and a few small arms from the battlefield at a time. The specific impacts may have appeared negligible in isolation, but the aggregation of effects is a valid consideration for the military objective test under the DoD Law of War Manual (sections 5.6.7.3 and 5.12.2.1). While this holistic approach is generally accepted, the scope of what may constitute an effective contribution or definite military advantage will rely on nuanced national understandings and policies and, in execution, on the good faith determinations by competent commanders for any specific attack (or broader operation). Therefore, in the space context–where proliferated constellations, often providing support to other warfighting capabilities (versus direct effects), are common–varying views on a particular commercial target and its value can exist among both allies and adversaries. Future Practice and U.S. Leadership International law develops through state practice, executed out of a sense of legal obligation (ICJ Statute, Article 38), and such practice can even inform established treaty text like that of the military objective test (Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties, Article 31). Therefore, even seemingly settled law may not be permanently so, and is ripe to be shaped or molded by States whose practice is frequent or significant in this domain. Beyond shaping the evolution of customary international law, non-binding norms can also have a significant impact on how States behave and what the international community views as legitimate. This creates an opportunity for U.S. leadership in shaping the expectations and norms of practice for what constitutes a legitimate military objective in outer space. A satisfactory answer to the question should not be answered by the law alone; the general law of armed conflict establishes what may be considered a lawful military objective, but it is for leaders, considering what is legal, ethical, and good policy, to factor in the whole picture—that is, what precedent do they want to set for the future of the domain? The United States needs to have a cogent position that takes into account more than just tactical or operational military advantage, and instead factors in what is in the holistic national interest and what makes for good, sustainable, and advantageous policy geared towards a predictable, stable domain in the future that enables all uses in the national interest: commercial, civil, scientific, and, of course, national security. Final Thoughts As noted at the outset, the law is a floor (not the ceiling) for protection of commercial objects. To the question of when commercial satellites are legitimate targets, the United States needs to determine what it wants the answer to be–both as a user of and potential neutralizer of others’ space assets–and actively pursue that as the rule through its practice and strategic communication. Following Secretary Meink’s speech, the CSO correctly noted that “[d]eterrence is strongest when we have a credible force and a resolve to do it,” and this announcement supports that credibility. Importantly, though, the CSO further noted that the Space Force must “make disciplined and responsible choices about how we build and sustain our combat advantage.” A race to the bottom, or minimum standards, is an option and may be expedient in some types of conflict and best serve the national interest, particularly in hostilities where a likely adversary poses a lower threat to or capacity to target U.S. space systems. If that is the case, the law as it stands will provide commanders with workable options and may be a “disciplined and responsible” choice. However, we are still in a period where the general rules as applied to the space domain can be shaped to national advantage and to create opportunities—and the United States should do so actively and with purpose, and factoring in the potential for adversaries with significant counter-space capabilities. If it wants more predictability (from law-abiding states) or, more likely, baseline rules to hold aggressors to account for violations, the United States should work towards norms and eventual rules to better shape understanding of “effective contribution” and “definite military advantage” for space systems. Determining thresholds and generally what is in or out of bounds in considering the lawful targeting of commercial satellites in conflict is a precedential matter the United States must take seriously, and with the understanding that U.S. military space activities may fall on both sides of the ledger.

candidates.full: SpaceX планирует до конца ноября запустить еще две группы спутников для Космических сил США. Миссии USSF-317 и USSF-226 намечены на 18 и 23 ноября соответственно. candidates.title: Google Project Zero will disclose bugs after 90 days, fixed or not
candidates.summary: Google Project Zero will disclose bugs after 90 days, fixed or not Google’s Project Zero will disclose the vulnerabilities it finds 90 days after reporting them to a vendor, whether or not the vendor has shipped a fix. The deadline drops to 60 days on February 2, 2027, and to 30 days on January 3, 2
candidates.full: Google Project Zero will disclose bugs after 90 days, fixed or not Google’s Project Zero will disclose the vulnerabilities it finds 90 days after reporting them to a vendor, whether or not the vendor has shipped a fix. The deadline drops to 60 days on February 2, 2027, and to 30 days on January 3, 2028. Project Zero calls the new policy “Full X,” where X is the number of days. The change ends the “90 + 30” rule the team has followed since 2021. That rule gave vendors up to 90 days to fix a bug, then another 30 days of “soak time” for the patch to roll out. The extra month is gone. A vendor that misses the deadline will see the technical details of an unfixed bug published. Why the clock is getting shorter Project Zero gives three reasons, and all three come back to large language models. First, LLMs help attackers find and exploit bugs faster. They also raise the odds that several parties, including malicious ones, find the same bug while it is under embargo. “A vulnerability reported today presents a much higher immediate risk to users than one reported last year,” Natalie Silvanovich of Project Zero wrote. Second, LLMs cut the time it takes to turn a patch into a working exploit. Project Zero now treats zero patch-to-exploitation time as “a reasonable, though imperfect, model of attacker behavior.” A patch already tells attackers where the bug is, and waiting a month to publish the details doesn’t change that. The team argues that this delay can put users at risk by giving them a false sense of secrecy. Project Zero wants vendors to shrink the patch gap. A vendor can close that gap by rolling out updates faster, or by protecting users some other way while the fix is on its way. Third, the volume has jumped. Project Zero is finding several vulnerabilities a week in targets where it once found a few a year. “Aspects of our policy that require vendor negotiation or agreement, including determining whether a bug is fixed and whether grace period applies, are quickly becoming unmanageable,” Silvanovich wrote. Three exceptions, no grace period Project Zero dropped most of its special cases, including the grace period and its variant policy. Three exceptions remain: - Vulnerabilities actively exploited in the wild fall under Google’s application security vulnerability disclosure policy. - If others have already published a bug’s details, Project Zero may publish its own details at its discretion. - A vendor can ask Project Zero to publish details of a bug it reported to that vendor. Hardware bugs may still get extra time. Project Zero has granted exceptions on rare occasions, including for Spectre and Meltdown, and says it will keep doing so. It still wants every vendor to plan how it would respond if a serious bug were about to be disclosed, including fixes that are not patches. Project Zero will not use severity to set disclosure dates. The team says it files only bugs with substantial severity and demonstrated security impact, though it admits its analysis isn’t always perfect. A bug’s severity changes its impact on users without changing how likely attackers are to find it. Vendors can still decide that some risks, such as unexploitable null pointer crashes, are acceptable for their users. A vendor’s severity rating will not move Project Zero’s disclosure date. The policy also assumes reports meet Project Zero’s standards for reproducibility, readability, reachability and impact, and the team says vendors can reasonably treat low-quality reports differently. The 30-day deadline waits until 2028 Before setting the schedule, Project Zero asked for feedback from the vendors it reports the most bugs to. Their main worry was that a sudden switch would hand unfixed bugs to attackers while vendors were still improving how they fix them. Vendors raised two other concerns. A harsh deadline could push them to fix Project Zero’s bugs first, even when other reported bugs were more severe. And vendors that could not meet an immediate deadline might stop trying. Project Zero says keeping a bug secret is worth less than it used to be, because attackers are more likely to find it during the embargo. It still sees some short-term value in the delay, and calls the staged schedule “challenging but realistic.” If you maintain software Project Zero tests, plan around January 3, 2028: from that date, details go public 30 days after the report, with no extra month for rollout. Fixed or not, the date holds Project Zero has long struggled to judge whether a bug counts as fixed, especially in code that isn’t shipped directly to users or isn’t publicly available. It was not unusual for the team to go back and forth with a vendor several times on one report before agreeing on a bug’s status. Vendors are starting to try fixes that aren’t patches, such as temporarily disabling code paths, and Project Zero expects that to make the judgment harder. “We still plan to track whether bugs are fixed and communicate if they are not, however, this will not be a decision point in our policy. This will enable us to share technical details of how users are protected without needing to make a binary judgement with consequences for the vendor,” Silvanovich concluded.

candidates.summary: Starshield restrictions help Russia’s energy attacks on Ukraine: Zelenskyy Starlink has recently denied restricting internet speeds but Elon Musk suggested the US military could be behind it. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said that speed restrictions by Starlink’s military-grade internet service
candidates.full: Starshield restrictions help Russia’s energy attacks on Ukraine: Zelenskyy Starlink has recently denied restricting internet speeds but Elon Musk suggested the US military could be behind it. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said that speed restrictions by Starlink’s military-grade internet service had aided a wave of deadly Russian attacks across Ukraine. Two people were killed on Saturday in a Russian drone attack on what Ukrainian officials called “critical infrastructure” in the northern Koriukivka region. An energy facility was also hit in Odesa overnight on Sunday, leaving 41,000 households without electricity, Ukraine’s DTEK energy provider said in a Telegram statement. Ukraine’s army said it shot down 106 of 132 Russian drones launched overnight. Zelenskyy posted on X that Russia was targeting energy substations with Shahed drones, which both sides commonly attack each other with. “And many of these strikes are getting through because restrictions on the operating speed of Starshield terminals along the front line and in the temporarily occupied territories are still there,” he posted, citing Starlink’s sister company and reiterating accusations that it was throttling internet speeds and hampering military operations. The president said on Saturday that the internet restrictions had been in place for five days and that Starlink reported technical problems, but Ukraine does “not believe that is the case”. It is the second such outage in recent weeks. Starlink, owned by US billionaire Elon Musk’s SpaceX, has denied restricting internet speeds. Last month, Musk said the United States government controls Starshield. Tit-for-tat attacks Russia’s Defence Ministry said on Sunday that it launched attacks targeting Ukraine’s military airfields, munitions depots and other military facilities. Authorities also said that an electrical engineer was killed and four others were injured in Russia’s Taganrog region after Ukrainian drones attacked the area on Sunday. Six people were injured in a drone attack in Nizhnekamsk, local officials said. The city, as well as the wider Trans-Kama region of Tatarstan, reported heavy Ukrainian attacks on industrial facilities and a residential building earlier on Sunday. US negotiators concluded visits to both countries in recent days in attempts to secure a ceasefire, despite tensions between Washington and Kyiv over Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries. Zelenskyy said the US floated the idea of Ukraine withdrawing its remaining forces from the eastern Donbas region in exchange for NATO membership. Russia’s President Vladimir Putin is due to meet President Donald Trump and China’s President Xi Jinping in the Chinese city of Shenzhen this week – but Ukraine is not on the agenda. Analysts have compared the meeting to the Yalta conference of 1945, which saw the US, UK and former Soviet Union divide Germany and establish the United Nations. However, in a statement on Sunday, Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha, dismissed Russia’s longstanding proposal to revise Europe’s security architecture. “Putin is throwing around ideas about reshaping the European security order. In his dreams, he sees himself in Yalta in 1945. The problem is that to put forward ideas of this magnitude, you first need to win a world war,” he said.

candidates.title: U.N. talks seek to rein in 'killer robots' as fears over AI weapons grow
candidates.summary: GENEVA — Negotiations on possible rules for the use of lethal autonomous weapons, also known as 'killer robots' are underway at the United Nations in Geneva. Supporters of controls on autonomous weapons say this week's U.N. conference on Certain Conventional Weapons (or CCW), which meets just once e
candidates.full: GENEVA — Negotiations on possible rules for the use of lethal autonomous weapons, also known as 'killer robots' are underway at the United Nations in Geneva. Supporters of controls on autonomous weapons say this week's U.N. conference on Certain Conventional Weapons (or CCW), which meets just once every five years, is the last best chance to agree rules before it is too late. Warfare technology has advanced rapidly in the last few years, with some experts warning that the world is just months away from having weapons that can choose targets and make the decision to kill autonomously. In Ukraine and Gaza, AI-assisted weapons have already been used to take out targets, with Ukrainian civilians reporting being 'hunted' by drones as they shop or go to school. But these are still controlled remotely by humans. Humanitarian organizations say the decision to kill – and responsibility for that choice – must stay in human hands. Ahead of this week's meeting, the United Nations, the International Committee of the Red Cross and the Pope have all called for legally binding rules. U.N. Secretary-General Antonio Guterres warned that allowing fully autonomous weapons to kill would be 'crossing a moral red line'. What are the risks? The Red Cross is especially worried that existing rules of war – the Geneva Conventions – cannot be fully respected by autonomous weapons. War is often chaotic and confusing, and the situation can change rapidly. Under the Conventions, soldiers who are wounded or in the process of surrendering can no longer be targeted. Georgia Haines, a legal adviser with the Red Cross, worries that autonomous weapons will not be able to distinguish between a soldier who is still fighting, one who is wounded and one who wants to surrender. 'The risk is that, based on the technology we are seeing, they are not able to understand in the same way that a human is the contextual signals. And so the risks are incredibly high that there will be a misidentification of a target.' Meanwhile, human rights groups warn that the technology behind AI-assisted weapons is becoming increasingly cheap and easy to use. The more it is adopted by the military, the greater the danger of proliferation and its use by terrorist groups or law enforcement agencies in repressive regimes. In theory, a swarm of autonomous drones could be programmed to kill everyone wearing a red sweater, everyone carrying a poster or even everyone speaking a certain language. Many of the countries now meeting in Geneva take such concerns very seriously. At least 50, including Ireland, Italy, Brazil, Mexico, France and Germany, are calling for a strict timetable to agree on binding rules governing autonomous weapons. But among states that are already developing and using semi-autonomous weapons, there is pushback. The United States, Russia and Israel have indicated they are set to oppose legally binding rules, with Washington proposing a five-year timetable to draft non-binding guidelines instead. The U.S. is traditionally a late adopter of international treaties. It did not ratify the Ottawa Convention on landmines, for example, although it did, over time, stop deploying them and reduce its stockpiles. Under President Trump, doubts about international law have grown. Washington has imposed sweeping sanctions on the International Criminal Court, and just this weekend, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, in a keynote speech to the Federalist Society, warned against "quoting laws to men with swords." The problem for states meeting in Geneva is that U.N. negotiations on limiting specific weapons are supposed to be conducted by consensus. This was achieved in 1995, when countries agreed to a ban on blinding lasers, but other agreements have proved elusive. With landmines, countries frustrated by the delay finally took negotiations outside the U.N. process to create the Ottawa Convention. This week, there may be a compromise: a longer or even open-ended negotiating period to come up with rules that individual states can adopt as binding or non-binding. For diplomats supporting such a solution, it is a way to ensure at least some progress. For campaigners, it is less than ideal, with one likening it to kicking a very dangerous can down the road. candidates.summary: TuringFonts is a simple technique for generate content (for websites or PDF files) that can't we crawled by bots or copied using the clipboard. It's useful in situations in which you want to publish some sensitive content that you don't want to be indexed by search engines like Google or Bing (such
candidates.full: TuringFonts is a simple technique for generate content (for websites or PDF files) that can't we crawled by bots or copied using the clipboard. It's useful in situations in which you want to publish some sensitive content that you don't want to be indexed by search engines like Google or Bing (such as e-mail addresses, telephone numbers or personal names) or when you don't want to allow the user to copy and paste your text (to avoid plagiarism or unauthorized modifications). This technique is based on the simple substitution cipher method and in the use of custom fonts. The simple substitutions cipher in a method of encoding in which each letter is replaced by another one. For example, you could decide to replace each letter by his neighbour in the alphabet (write 'b' instead of 'a', 'c' instead of 'b', etc.), in that case the text "Hello" would be write as "Ifmmp". A font (in computing) is basically a file that indicates how to draw each letter. So, for example, some fonts define that the letter 'O' must be draw rounded while others indicate that must be oval. So basically you encrypt your text using some substitution cipher and then you apply (to that text) a Turing font that inverses the substitution previously made. A Turing font is a font whose symbols has been unordered on purpose. So when a letter is found, another letter is draw in his place. For example, a Turing font may indicate to draw an 'a' when encountering a 'b', draw a 'b' when encountering a 'c', etc.). In that's way any bot or computer, that get access to your website or PDF file, is going to read the encrypted text while all humans visitors are going to read the original text. Write some text here: This is what all computers and bots are going to read: {{encrypText}} This is what all humans are going to see*: (*) Try selecting and copying this text into a notepad to see what happens Have some doubt? Check the live demo or download the sample PDF file. In order to use this technique, you must follow a two step process: - Encode you text using some substitution method. You can use this encoder to do it. - Apply, to the previous text, a Turing font. In the download section you can find a list of fonts ready to be used. If you want to use your own substitution alphabets and/or generate your own Turing fonts, I recommend you to read the advanced topics. Download font Select a font, a substitution method and download the corresponding TTF file. Install font Install the downloaded font into your computer. Encode text Encode your text using the substitution method previously chosen. Apply font Copy the encoded text into a word processor and apply the font installed. Verify Verify that the text can be read and export the document as PDF (indicating that the fonts used must be embedded). Select a font, a substitution method and download the corresponding Zip file. Unzip the file in one of your website's folder. Declare font Declare the selected font in the CSS code of the page in which you are going to use it. Copy the encoded text into the page and apply the font. Verify that the text can be read. In this section you will find a list of Turing fonts ready to be used. Each row of the table contains a font type, and each column indicates the substitution algorithm used for generate the font. For each combination, you can download either a TTF file or a ZIP file (containing the font in all the required formats to be used at the web). | | ROT13 | Atbash | Zebra | |---|---|---|---| | Arial | | | | | Courier New | | | | | Georgia | | | | | Tahoma | | | | | Verdana | | | | More fonts may be added if you gently ask for them. candidates.full: Von Alan Moore Als der kanadische Premierminister Mark Carney beschloss, russischen Spielern die Visa für die im nächsten Monat stattfindende Eishockey-Juniorenweltmeisterschaft zu verweigern , wurde er zum ersten gewählten Regierungschef, der sich offen über ein Gerichtsurteil sowie die Entscheidung eines internationalen Sportverbandes hinwegsetzte. Damit entfesselte er gefährliche und aggressive antirussische Kräfte im eigenen Land und warf die Sportdiplomatie um mehr als 50 Jahre zurück. In der Woche zuvor, am 30. Oktober, hatte der Internationale Sportgerichtshof (CAS) entschieden , russische und weißrussische Mannschaften wieder zu internationalen Wettbewerben zuzulassen. Die Internationale Eishockey-Föderation (IIHF) akzeptierte diesen Beschluss, während zahlreiche nationale Verbände in Europa erwartungsgemäß reagierten. Acht Länder, darunter Lettland und Frankreich, kündigten an, Spiele gegen Russland zu boykottieren. Deutschland, Gastgeber der IIHF-Weltmeisterschaft 2027, äußerte zwar Bedenken, akzeptierte aber die Rückkehr Russlands; lediglich die Slowakei begrüßte sie. Sponsoren der Veranstaltung in Deutschland haben sich entweder zurückgezogen oder mit einem solchen Schritt gedroht. Was in dieser gesamten "Diskussion" völlig zu kurz kommt, ist die Meinung der Eishockey-Fans. Nicht die der NATO-Trolle und Online-Bots, die gegen alles Russische hetzen und wüten. Auch nicht die Meinung jener Handvoll kanadischer Ukrainer, die in Ottawa gegen den Besuch der Washington Capitals – des Teams des russischen Stars Alexander Owetschkin – protestierten. Und schon gar nicht die effekthascherischen Äußerungen von Politikern oder den von ihnen abhängigen Sportfunktionären. Die Stimmen der tatsächlichen Eishockey-Fans werden von den Medien geflissentlich ignoriert – ebenso wie die Gefahr, die von einer Teilnahme russischer oder weißrussischer Mannschaften an internationalen Wettbewerben ausgehen könnte. "Es ist reiner Hass auf Russen" Im Oktober war ich im Rahmen einer Geschäftsreise für Capital Sports in verschiedenen EU-Ländern unterwegs. Ich berichtete von einer Reihe bedeutender Sportereignisse und führte Interviews mit Athleten und Funktionären; in Deutschland, Italien und Litauen stand dabei das Eishockey im Mittelpunkt. "Früher habe ich mir sehr gerne Spiele der KHL (der in Russland beheimateten Kontinentalen Hockey-Liga) angesehen. Sie sind zwar nicht so brutal wie in Kanada, aber das spielerische Niveau ist beeindruckend", erzählte mir Nils, ein Fan der Iserlohn Roosters, in Köln. "Man merkt den Unterschied deutlich, jetzt wo keine russische Mannschaft mehr [bei Weltmeisterschaften oder Olympischen Spielen] antritt. Für die Spieler ist das eine harte Situation, zumal ihre Karriere ohnehin nur kurz ist." Nils und sein Freund Patrick waren für das Spiel ihrer Mannschaft gegen die Kölner Haie in der Stadt. Ich sprach mit Dutzenden von Zuschauern, die das Spiel am 1. November besuchten – keine zwei Tage nach der Entscheidung des Internationalen Sportgerichtshofs. Der Deutsche Eishockey-Bund (DEB) hatte bereits seine Ablehnung zum Ausdruck gebracht , und in den sozialen Medien kursierten Gerüchte über Boykotte und Schlimmeres. Patrick und ich stießen auf einen gemeinsamen Nenner. "Wenn sie von 'Sicherheit' sprechen, dann haben sie damit recht. Denn wir sehen ja jetzt, dass sie [proukrainische Akteure] für jede Menge Ärger sorgen können – und das nicht nur im Internet." Begriffe wie Sicherheit (im Sinne von Schutz und Unversehrtheit) tauchten in den Stellungnahmen der meisten nationalen Verbände auf – und das aus gutem Grund. Wir haben bereits gesehen, wozu Kiew in anderen souveränen Staaten fähig ist, wenn es darum geht, ein Signal zu setzen. Ob der versuchte Mord an einem im Exil lebenden ukrainischen Oligarchen in Monaco oder das in Deutschland laufende Verfahren gegen einen ukrainischen Militärangehörigen im Zusammenhang mit dem Terroranschlag auf Nord Stream – es gibt durchaus Grund zur Sorge. "Diese Leute [Politiker und Sportfunktionäre] sind Idioten. Es ist reiner Hass auf Russen", sagte Mikaela aus Düsseldorf, die schon ihr ganzes Leben lang Eishockey-Fan ist. "Wir hatten jetzt genug Krieg, es muss sich etwas ändern. Ich meine, schauen wir uns den Fußball an [FIFA-Weltmeisterschaft 2026]: Die US-Amerikaner durften das Turnier ausrichten, obwohl sie kleine Mädchen in einer Schule in die Luft gejagt haben", sagte Mikaela in Anspielung auf den Raketenangriff vom 28. Februar 2026 im iranischen Minab. Ihr Freund brachte jedoch ein Szenario ins Spiel, das an den Vorfall mit Nord Stream erinnert. "Kannst du garantieren, dass sie nicht eine Arena in die Luft jagen? Ich kann es nicht", sagte er, fügte aber sogleich hinzu: "Ich möchte aber, dass Weißrussland und Russland wieder mitspielen können. Ohne dass sie schikaniert werden." "Der Fußball muss Rückgrat zeigen und Russland wieder einbinden" Vier Tage später in Italien – während ich bei der UEFA-Europa-League-Partie zwischen der AC Mailand und Ferencváros vor Ort war – hatte sich die Lage im Eishockey deutlicher herauskristallisiert. Schweden, Finnland, Tschechien, Frankreich, Österreich, Norwegen, Dänemark und Lettland waren bereit, finanzielle Einbußen in Kauf zu nehmen, anstatt gegen Russland anzutreten. Das von Carney verhängte Einreiseverbot für russische Nachwuchssportler war zu diesem Zeitpunkt zwei Tage alt, und die Fans aus Mailand sowie die Gäste aus Budapest nahmen kein Blatt vor den Mund. "Das ist doch Bullshit", sagte Nico, ein 24-jähriger Fan der Mailänder Fußball- und Eishockey-Teams, in der Halbzeitpause. "Ich kann diese Leute und ihre Doppelmoral nicht ausstehen. Israel – okay. Ukraine – okay. Sie dürfen mitspielen, während Kinder getötet werden – alles kein Problem. Aber Russland? Die Spieler sind doch nicht diejenigen, die da kämpfen. Sollen doch diese fetten Dummköpfe, die unbedingt Krieg wollen, selbst an die Front gehen – die Spieler sollen einfach spielen dürfen." Andere Milan-Fans äußerten sich ähnlich; einer von ihnen zog einen Vergleich zum Fußball. "Ich war für ein Spiel [der UEFA Champions League 2012] in Russland, und meine Frau und ich haben uns in St. Petersburg verliebt. Wir sind 2018 zur Weltmeisterschaft wieder hingefahren – ich liebe die Kultur dort. Der Fußball muss endlich Rückgrat zeigen und Russland wieder zurückholen. Schluss mit diesem sinnlosen Hass und den Blockaden. Wir sind doch alle Menschen. Wir sind alle nur Menschen", sagte Andrea. Er zeigte stolz Fotos von seinen Aufenthalten in Russland und meinte, er würde wieder dorthin reisen, "sobald diese ganze dumme Schießerei aufhört". Auf das kanadische Visumverbot angesprochen, lachte er nur: "Das zeigt doch bloß, dass sie nicht in der Lage sind, Kinder vor durchgeknallten Psychopathen zu schützen – mehr steckt nicht dahinter." János, einer der Anführer der Ultras von Ferencváros, schloss sich Andreas Ansicht an. "Die Eishockey-Verantwortlichen haben Mut bewiesen, indem sie Russland wieder am Spielbetrieb teilnehmen ließen ... Mir gefällt nicht, was sie in der Ukraine tun, aber ich weiß auch, was die Ukraine meinem Volk dort [den ethnischen Ungarn] antut. In keinem Krieg gibt es eine gute Seite, doch wir haben in Europa weitaus größere Probleme, um die wir uns kümmern müssen, als einander zu bekämpfen." "Sollen sie doch alle ablehnen und verlieren" Zurück in Vilnius berichtete mir am Mittwoch ein hochrangiger Funktionär des litauischen Eishockeyverbands (LIHF) von dem Druck, dem sie ausgesetzt sind – auch wenn sie in absehbarer Zeit gar nicht gegen Russland spielen werden. Die Person, die anonym bleiben wollte, sprach von einem enormen politischen Druck, "ein Zeichen der Solidarität mit unserem Nachbarn [Lettland] zu setzen". Der Funktionär erklärte, dass sowohl ihr wichtigster Geldgeber – das Ministerium für Bildung, Wissenschaft und Sport – als auch mindestens ein Sponsor, das Immobilienunternehmen "Ober Haus" (tätig im Baltikum), von ihnen verlangt hätten, sich an die Seite Lettlands zu stellen, das sich für einen Boykott ausgesprochen hatte, sollte Russland an der WM nächstes Jahr in Deutschland teilnehmen. "Ich persönlich würde sagen: Sollen sie doch alle das Spiel verweigern und die Partien verlieren. Genau wie Kanada: Sie sollten die russischen Jungs ausschließen und das Turnier in ein Land verlegen, in dem die Leute noch ihren Verstand benutzen." Carney und seine Regierung haben angekündigt, sich über das Urteil des Internationalen Sportgerichtshofs (CAS) hinwegzusetzen und Spielern oder Betreuern, die über ein gültiges Visum verfügen, die Teilnahme zu verweigern. Die Regierung Carney hat in diesem Jahr 116 in Russland geborenen Spielern Visa erteilt. Derzeit spielen neun Russen für NHL-Teams in Kanada. Von den sieben dort ansässigen Mannschaften haben nur Ottawa und Vancouver aktuell keine Russen in ihrem aktiven Kader – wobei beide Vereine dennoch russische Spieler unter Vertrag haben. Carney befindet sich in einer schwierigen persönlichen und beruflichen Lage. Beruflich ist er auf die Stimmen der großen ukrainischen Diaspora angewiesen – von denen viele den Nazikollaborateur Stepan Bandera verehren und Russland sowie die Russen hassen. Persönlich ist er der Taufpate des Sohnes von Chrystia Freeland. Freeland, deren Großvater mütterlicherseits, Michael Chomiak, ebenfalls ein Nazikollaborateur war, arbeitet heute in Kiew als "Wirtschaftsberaterin" für Wladimir Selenskij. Der russische Eishockeyverband hat die IIHF zum Handeln aufgefordert: Kanada solle entweder dazu bewegt werden, russische Kinder mitspielen zu lassen, oder das Turnier müsse verlegt werden. Laut dem litauischen Funktionär ist Letzteres am wahrscheinlichsten. "Kanada kann nicht zurückweichen, und die IIHF ist besorgt wegen möglicher Terroranschläge." Dieses Szenario, so die Einschätzung, könnte sie zum Handeln zwingen. "Man muss wissen, dass in Alberta – wo der Wettbewerb vom 26. Dezember bis zum 5. Januar stattfinden soll – viele Ukrainer leben. Es ist durchaus denkbar, dass es zu Angriffen auf russische Spieler oder zu Bombendrohungen kommt; mehr braucht es nicht, um die Situation eskalieren zu lassen." Die Entscheidungsgewalt liegt ganz bei der IIHF. Sie könnte das Turnier aus Kanada abziehen und in die USA verlegen. Zwar mag die Sorge bestehen, dass nationale Verbände sich abspalten und eine neue Weltorganisation gründen könnten – doch die Wahrscheinlichkeit dafür ist verschwindend gering; sie ist in etwa so hoch wie die Überlebenschance eines Eiswürfels in einem Vulkan. Es bleibt abzuwarten, ob die Sportfunktionäre und Politiker auf die Öffentlichkeit hören und erkennen, dass sie jetzt einen historischen Schritt tun können, um ihren Sport – und die Welt – zu retten. Denn Sportdiplomatie ist heute wichtiger denn je. Diejenigen, die andere mobben, dürfen nicht gewinnen – auch abseits des Eises nicht. Übersetzt aus dem Englischen . Alan Moore ist Sportjournalist und Moderator von Capital Sports 3.0. Er lebt in Vilnius. Als ehemaliger Sportler hat er mehr als 30 Jahre Erfahrung im Profisport.

candidates.full: Components of the European FREYA missile defense system, currently known: ▪️ FP-7.X interceptor missile manufactured by the Ukrainian company Fire Point. It is based on the Soviet 48N6 missile originally designed for the S-300PM air defense system; ▪️/ Mobile launch system manufactured in Ukraine. The chassis used for the launch system is unknown, but it may also be European, like the rest of the system; ▪️ Detection radar manufactured by the German company Hensoldt. The TRML-4D radar, also used in the IRIS-T air defense system, is expected to be supplied and integrated; ▪️ Tracking radar manufactured by the Danish company Weibel. The GFTR-2100/48 radar is expected to be supplied and integrated; ▪️ Command and control center manufactured by the Norwegian company Kongsberg, also used in the NASAMS air defense system; ▪️ Combined guidance system (semi-active radar + infrared) manufactured by the German company Diehl Defence, which produces them for the IRIS-T missile defense system. Currently, only the readiness of the missile itself (without the guidance system), the launch system for it, and the tracking radar have been confirmed. The detection radar, the command and control center, and the guidance system are not ready. In addition to the components mentioned above, alternative options are also being considered. For detection, radars such as the Swedish Giraffe from Saab or the French Ground Master 400 from Thales could be used. For tracking, the Italian KRONOS Land from Leonardo could be used. The use of communication systems from the Spanish company Sener and optoelectronics from the French company Safran has also been discussed. It is possible that in the future, the FREYA missile defense system will be modular and configurable to meet the specific needs of a particular customer. ▪️IF, of course, it ever reaches mass production.

candidates.full: Більше, ніж просто солодке. Вчені з’ясували, як мед впливає на клітинне старіння Вчені виявили нову корисну властивість меду (Фото: PollyDot/pixabay) Італійські вчені виявили, що поліфлорний мед здатний посилювати природні захисні механізми клітин шкіри та зменшувати наслідки впливу ультрафіолету. У майбутньому ця властивість може знайти застосування в косметології та дерматології. Ультрафіолетове випромінювання — одна з основних причин передчасного старіння шкіри. Сонячні промені пошкоджують клітини, провокують окиснювальний стрес і підвищують ризик розвитку раку шкіри. Однак дослідники з Університету Сассарі в Італії з’ясували, що поліфлорний мед може допомагати клітинам протистояти такому впливу. Мед давно відомий своїми антиоксидантними, протизапальними та ранозагоювальними властивостями. Спеціальні медичні засоби на його основі вже застосовують для лікування опіків і складних ран. Як мед впливає на клітини шкіри Для експерименту вчені створили лабораторну модель шкіри людини. Частину клітин протягом 48 годин обробляли 1%-м розчином поліфлорного меду, після чого піддавали дії ультрафіолету. З’ясувалося, що оброблені медом клітини демонстрували більш виражені захисні реакції. Дослідники зафіксували підвищення антиоксидантної активності, посилення експресії генів, пов’язаних із відновленням тканин, а також зниження активності певних маркерів старіння. За словами дослідниці Фікіє Фульї Кавак, мед допомагав клітинам підтримувати баланс між захистом від пошкоджень і процесами оновлення. Чи може мед замінити сонцезахисний крем? Попри перспективні результати, науковці наголошують, що дослідження проводилося виключно в лабораторних умовах. Наразі невідомо, чи справляє мед аналогічну дію безпосередньо на шкіру людини. Не можна використовувати мед замість сонцезахисного крему, оскільки його ефективність у захисті від UVA- та UVB-випромінювання клінічно не доведена. Наразі фахівці продовжують вивчати механізми дії меду та розробляють спеціальні нановолокнисті матеріали для доставки його активних компонентів. У майбутньому такі технології можуть стати основою нових косметичних засобів, спрямованих на захист шкіри від негативного впливу навколишнього середовища. Правова інформація. Ця стаття містить загальні відомості довідкового характеру і не повинна розглядатися як альтернатива рекомендаціям лікаря. NV не несе відповідальності за будь-який діагноз, поставлений читачем на основі матеріалів сайту. NV також не несе відповідальності за зміст інших інтернет-ресурсів, посилання на які присутні в цій статті. Якщо вас турбує стан вашого здоров’я, зверніться до лікаря.

Источник: Bloomberg Беспилотные автомобили Zoox будут автоматически предлагать пользователям Uber при заказе поездок в категориях UberX, Uber Comfort и Uber Electric без дополнительной платы, рассказали компании. candidates.full: Компания впервые подключила к своей платформе роботакси без водительского места. Источник: Bloomberg Беспилотные автомобили Zoox будут автоматически предлагать пользователям Uber при заказе поездок в категориях UberX, Uber Comfort и Uber Electric без дополнительной платы, рассказали компании. Uber впервые подключил к своей платформе роботакси без водительского места, Zoox — предоставила доступ к своему автопарку через сторонний сервис, пишет The Verge. При этом заказать Zoox по-прежнему можно и через собственное приложение компании. Пока сервис работает только в туристических районах Лас-Вегаса. До конца 2026 года Zoox планирует начать работу в Лос-Анджелесе, интеграцию с Uber добавят в 2027-м. Кроме того, Uber и Zoox заключили партнёрство с компанией MGM Resorts International, управляющей отелями и казино в Лас-Вегасе. В рамках сотрудничества они адаптируют зоны посадки и высадки пассажиров для роботакси и улучшат навигацию на территории отелей. Amazon приобрёл разработчика машин-беспилотников Zoox в июне 2020 года. В 2025 году компания запустила бесплатные поездки для всех пользователей в Лас-Вегасе. Роботакси от Zoox разгоняется до 75 миль/час (около 120 км/час) и может перевозить до четырёх пассажиров. Электромобиль умеет двигаться в любом направлении: у него нет кабины водителя, поэтому ему не нужно разворачиваться. #новости #uber #amazon #zoox

candidates.title: Common genetic variants matter more in Alzheimer’s than scientists thought
candidates.summary: An international genetic study of more than 2.8 million people has identified 127 regions of human DNA associated with Alzheimer’s disease, including 48 regions linked to the condition for the first time. candidates.full: An international genetic study of more than 2.8 million people has identified 127 regions of human DNA associated with Alzheimer’s disease, including 48 regions linked to the condition for the first time. Published in Nature, the research indicates that common inherited variants account for nearly three times as much of the population variation in Alzheimer’s risk as previous estimates suggested. The findings also connect genetic susceptibility to heightened gene activity in brain immune cells alongside dampened gene activity in nerve cells. Alzheimer’s disease is a progressive brain disorder that gradually erodes memory, reasoning, and everyday functioning, accounting for most dementia cases worldwide. Existing disease-modifying drugs mainly aim to remove sticky clumps of amyloid-beta protein from brain tissue, yet they tend to offer modest symptom relief. Because twin studies indicate that inherited differences account for 60% to 80% of the variation in Alzheimer’s risk, researchers use genome-wide association studies, scanning millions of common single-letter DNA variations across populations to find chromosomal regions, called loci, linked to the illness. Larger samples have steadily expanded that map. For example, a 2021 genetic study of more than 1.1 million people was led by several of the same researchers, including co-lead author Douglas Wightman, and shared several cohorts with the new work. That analysis uncovered seven new risk regions and highlighted microglia, the specialized immune cells in the brain and spinal cord that engulf debris and respond to injury. Soon after, a 2022 genome-wide study of nearly 790,000 individuals, which also shared several co-authors and datasets with the current study, mapped 75 risk regions and brought the total number of known Alzheimer’s loci to roughly 80. Even with dozens of risk regions mapped, statistical tallies of heritability suggested that common DNA variants explained only about 5% of population differences in risk, fueling doubts that much genetic risk remained to be found beyond APOE, a major risk gene that transports cholesterol and fats in the brain. The authors of a 2020 genetic modeling study argued that late-onset Alzheimer’s might involve fewer than 100 common causal variants in total, implying gene discovery had nearly plateaued. Other models predicted roughly 1,200 contributing regions, prompting study co-lead authors Emil Uffelmann and Douglas P. Wightman, researchers in the Complex Trait Genetics lab at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, and their colleagues to test how much common genetic risk remained hidden. “The main goal of our study was locus discovery: identifying variants and genes that affect the risk of developing Alzheimer’s disease,” Uffelmann told PsyPost. “Each new discovery provides clues about the causes of the disease and may lead to new treatments in the future. Another, more academic, motivating factor was to address the conundrum of low heritability estimates.” The team pooled data across 30 cohorts totaling more than 2.8 million participants: 109,479 diagnosed Alzheimer’s cases, 74,141 proxy cases, 2,131,799 controls, and 499,708 proxy controls. Because Alzheimer’s typically emerges after age 65, many biobank volunteers are too young to show symptoms, so genotyped adults who reported a parent with Alzheimer’s or dementia served as proxy cases, weighted to reflect the half of parental DNA that children inherit. Measured by effective sample size, which weights cohorts by their balance of cases and controls, the dataset was 91% European, 5% African, 3% East Asian, and under 1% each of admixed American and South Asian ancestry. Across the cohorts, the team analyzed more than 8.1 million common DNA variants, adjusting for age, sex, genetic ancestry, and study-specific factors while excluding cases diagnosed before age 40 where possible to avoid rare single-gene forms of the disease. Researchers then combined the genetic map with machine-learning tools, single-cell brain RNA atlases, and regulatory drug databases to identify likely causal genes, relevant cell types, and drug interactions. Analysis code and summary statistics, excluding proprietary 23andMe data, were posted publicly. Across all meta-analyses, the researchers identified 127 distinct genetic regions associated with Alzheimer’s disease, consisting of 118 in the multi-ancestry analysis and nine additional regions in the European-only analysis. Forty-eight regions were newly identified, while associations on the X chromosome, tested in a smaller effective sample of 196,822 compared with 416,493 overall, were not statistically significant. Ancestry-specific scans detected 114 regions in European, three in African, and two in East Asian groups, whereas associations in the smaller South Asian and admixed American samples were not statistically significant. A subset with direct clinical diagnoses rather than parental proxies included 20,402 female cases and 15,689 male cases, with 261,889 and 214,956 controls respectively. Inherited risk overlapped closely between men and women. However, the high-risk ε4 variant of APOE carried a modestly stronger association with Alzheimer’s disease in women than in men, about 13% stronger. Comparing the genetic findings against single-cell RNA data from donated brain tissue showed that genetic risk concentrated in genes expressed at higher levels in microglia and lower levels in neurons, the nerve cells that transmit electrical and chemical signals across the brain, in people with Alzheimer’s compared with unaffected donors. Three neuronal subtypes initially stood out, including two types of inhibitory, or signal-braking, neurons that produce somatostatin or small signaling peptides and are known to be vulnerable early in Alzheimer’s. After adjusting for average expression changes across all brain cell types, however, the microglial link held firm while the individual subtype signals weakened, indicating broader neuronal dampening. The authors suggest that inherited risk variants may push microglial immune genes toward overactivity while lowering gene expression in vulnerable neurons, though they note it remains uncertain whether neuronal dampening is an initial trigger or a downstream consequence of pathology. Pathway analyses reinforced roles for immune activation, fat binding, cell adhesion, and amyloid clearance, alongside five processes new to Alzheimer’s genetic scans, including oxidative-stress regulation via glutathione metabolism and membrane recycling at nerve junctions. Using a statistical model that accommodates APOE’s large impact alongside functional DNA features, the team estimated that common variants account for 16% of population differences in underlying susceptibility to Alzheimer’s among people of European ancestry, assuming a 5% lifetime prevalence. That heritability estimate is nearly triple the 6% figure from an older regression method that simulations indicated understates heritability when one gene dominates, while African-ancestry heritability estimates were not statistically significant given smaller samples and greater genetic diversity. Combined into a polygenic score, a single number summarizing inherited risk across millions of DNA variants, the predictors explained nearly 13% of the variation in disease susceptibility on average across held-out European cohorts, outperforming APOE status alone. Among European-ancestry UK Biobank adults aged 65 and older, Alzheimer’s prevalence was seven times higher in the top 10% of polygenic scores than in the bottom 10%, and three times higher than the whole-sample average. Uffelmann offered a sharper version of the same comparison: “Thinking about genetic risk in absolute terms may be useful. We found that, on average, 1 in 20 participants aged 65 years or older in the UK Biobank were diagnosed with Alzheimer’s disease. In people with the highest genetic risk (top 1%), the fraction of Alzheimer’s cases increased to almost 1 in 4. Clearly, genetics plays an important role in affecting risk, but it does not determine diagnosis.” Cross-referencing newly prioritized genes with regulatory databases identified 17 genes in the new regions that interact with approved non-Alzheimer’s medications. Compounds targeting three of those genes showed promise in earlier animal studies of Alzheimer’s, whereas drugs targeting two others failed to ease symptoms in prior mouse or human tests. Within a known risk region, the team’s model newly prioritized QPCT, which encodes an enzyme that modifies amyloid-beta into the specific form targeted by the approved Alzheimer’s antibody drug donanemab. A newly identified region spanning UBE2V1 and SPATA2, genes involved in protein clumping and programmed cell death, had previously been linked to both amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and frontotemporal dementia, and shared a likely causal variant between Alzheimer’s disease and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. These results align with an earlier multi-ancestry genetic analysis of clinically diagnosed and family-history cases, which uncovered 16 novel Alzheimer’s risk regions and linked several to altered brain gene expression. The cellular pattern also echoes an earlier post-mortem brain tissue study. Although that work measured active gene expression after death rather than inherited DNA variants across populations, it similarly pointed to heightened inflammatory activity in microglia paired with reduced signaling gene expression in neurons in Alzheimer’s disease. There are a few things to keep in mind when interpreting these findings. Although public and nonprofit grants primarily funded the work, several co-authors are employed by or hold stock in pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, including Roche, Regeneron, Amgen deCODE genetics, Janssen, Bayer, and Eli Lilly, which makes donanemab. Co-author Kaj Blennow became an Eli Lilly employee in September 2025. Several other authors have served as paid consultants or advisors to drugmakers developing Alzheimer’s treatments. More than 90% of the effective sample also came from people of European descent, which limited locus discovery in underrepresented groups and made polygenic scores far less accurate in African and East Asian cohorts. Roughly 40% of all cases, and 62% to 82% in non-European groups, relied on self-reported parental dementia history rather than clinical diagnoses, potentially blending Alzheimer’s with other late-life dementias. Finally, a genetic link or drug-database match does not mean targeting a gene will safely slow cognitive decline, and polygenic scores remain probabilistic estimates rather than diagnoses, pointing to the need for laboratory experiments and more diverse clinical cohorts. Stepping back, Uffelmann emphasized that inherited DNA is one piece of a broader health picture. “Genetics plays an important role in Alzheimer’s risk and points mostly to immune involvement, chiefly through microglia, the brain’s resident immune cells,” he said. “Yet it’s only part of the story, and lifestyle and environmental factors also matter.” The study, “Alzheimer’s disease genetics converges on microglial and neuronal dysregulation,” was authored by Emil Uffelmann, Douglas P. candidates.full: Components of the European FREYA missile defense system, currently known: ▪️ FP-7.X interceptor missile manufactured by the Ukrainian company Fire Point. It is based on the Soviet 48N6 missile originally designed for the S-300PM air defense system; ▪️/ Mobile launch system manufactured in Ukraine. The chassis used for the launch system is unknown, but it may also be European, like the rest of the system; ▪️ Detection radar manufactured by the German company Hensoldt. The TRML-4D radar, also used in the IRIS-T air defense system, is expected to be supplied and integrated; ▪️ Tracking radar manufactured by the Danish company Weibel. The GFTR-2100/48 radar is expected to be supplied and integrated; ▪️ Command and control center manufactured by the Norwegian company Kongsberg, also used in the NASAMS air defense system; ▪️ Combined guidance system (semi-active radar + infrared) manufactured by the German company Diehl Defence, which produces them for the IRIS-T missile defense system. Currently, only the readiness of the missile itself (without the guidance system), the launch system for it, and the tracking radar have been confirmed. The detection radar, the command and control center, and the guidance system are not ready. In addition to the components mentioned above, alternative options are also being considered. For detection, radars such as the Swedish Giraffe from Saab or the French Ground Master 400 from Thales could be used. For tracking, the Italian KRONOS Land from Leonardo could be used. The use of communication systems from the Spanish company Sener and optoelectronics from the French company Safran has also been discussed. It is possible that in the future, the FREYA missile defense system will be modular and configurable to meet the specific needs of a particular customer. ▪️IF, of course, it ever reaches mass production.

candidates.full: #ЭпохаПутина В России заработали научные установки, каких раньше в стране не было. ⠀ В Дубне построили коллайдер NICA. Он разгоняет ядра атомов почти до скорости света и сталкивает их. Так учёные воссоздают условия первых мгновений после Большого взрыва и изучают, как появилось вещество, из которого состоит всё вокруг. Поэтому NICA называют «машиной времени». ⠀ Есть у коллайдера и прикладная польза: ▪️ электроника, которая выдерживает радиацию, — для спутников и космических кораблей; ▪️ защита космонавтов от излучения в дальних полётах; ▪️ новые материалы и изучение того, как радиация действует на живые клетки. ⠀ Владимир Путин осуществил технологический пуск NICA в июне 2024 года. В феврале в кольцах коллайдера впервые одновременно пошли встречные пучки. ⠀ Под Новосибирском достраивают синхротрон СКИФ. Это огромный «рентген» с кольцом радиусом 476 метров. На нём будут изучать новые материалы, лекарства и катализаторы. Первый эксперимент запланирован на конец ноября.

candidates.full: Российские власти обещают жилье и помощь с переездом ученым, готовым работать на Дальнем Востоке. При этом после 2022 года научные организации региона все активнее вовлекаются в выполнение военных заказов. Университеты разрабатывают беспилотники и наземных роботов для армии, региональные власти выделяют деньги на оборонные исследования, а ученым приходится откладывать собственные проекты. T-invariant выяснил , как война изменила работу дальневосточных лабораторий, почему гражданские исследования уступают место военным заказам и как сотрудничество с оборонной промышленностью влияет на научную карьеру. НАСТОЯЩИЙ МАТЕРИАЛ ПРОИЗВЕДЕН, РАСПРОСТРАНЕН И НАПРАВЛЕН ИНОСТРАННЫМ АГЕНТОМ T-INVARIANT, ЛИБО КАСАЕТСЯ ДЕЯТЕЛЬНОСТИ ИНОСТРАННОГО АГЕНТА T-INVARIANT. 18+ В одной из дальневосточных университетских лабораторий после начала войны оборудование, предназначенное для научных экспериментов, передали под испытания для предприятия, выполнявшего оборонный заказ. Исследования пришлось переносить, а от части экспериментов отказаться. К 2023 году подобные заказы стали поступать регулярно. «Фундаментальный проект необязательно закрывать. Его можно просто постоянно откладывать», — объясняет исследовательница научной политики Анна. Военные разработки постепенно становятся частью университетской работы. В Бурятии исследования в интересах СВО включили в конкурс научных грантов. В Хабаровске студенческое конструкторское бюро создает беспилотники по военным техническим заданиям, в Забайкалье разработанных студентами роботов передают армии. На Сахалине производство военных квадрокоптеров разместили на территории научной организации. Меняются и условия научной карьеры. Результаты исследований приходится согласовывать с промышленными заказчиками, часть данных нельзя публиковать. Молодые ученые получают доступ к оборудованию и финансированию, но рискуют остаться без научных публикаций и возможности самостоятельно выбирать темы. При этом отказаться от военного заказа формально можно. Один из собеседников T-invariant рассказал, что его коллега после такого отказа сохранил работу, но перестал получать приглашения к участию в оплачиваемых промышленных проектах. В полном материале на нашем сайте — о милитаризации дальневосточной науки, распределении государственного финансирования и о том, почему обещанных зарплат и жилья может оказаться недостаточно, чтобы привлечь ученых в регион. —————————————— ▶ Материал целиком на нашем сайте / Наши материалы также доступны на английском языке / @t_invariant — медиа о науке во время войны Подписаться

candidates.full: Amazon a pierdut 40 de sateliți destinați viitoarei sale rețele de internet, după ce o rachetă Vulcan a eșuat la aproximativ zece minute de la lansare, transmite Mediafax. Incidentul s-a produs duminică, în Florida, și reprezintă primul eșec al unei misiuni pentru United Launch Alliance (ULA). Racheta a decolat de la baza Cape Canaveral, transportând sateliți ai rețelei Amazon Leo, proiectul prin care gigantul american încearcă să concureze serviciul Starlink al lui Elon Musk. La zece minute de la lansare, vehiculul a suferit o defecțiune și nu a mai reușit să plaseze încărcătura pe orbită, anunță Reuters. „Confirmăm că vehiculul Vulcan, lansat de la Complexul 41, a suferit o anomalie la zece minute de la începutul zborului și nu a reușit să transporte misiunea Amazon pe orbită”, a transmis ULA. Cauza defecțiunii nu a fost stabilită. Compania a anunțat deschiderea unei investigații tehnice, care ar putea întârzia luni întregi următoarele lansări. United Launch Alliance a fost înființată în 2006, prin reunirea programelor de rachete Delta și Atlas ale Boeing și Lockheed Martin. Până la incidentul de duminică, toate misiunile companiei își îndepliniseră obiectivele de lansare. Pentru Vulcan, noua rachetă principală a ULA, era al cincilea zbor de la debutul din 2024. Racheta revenise în activitate după o pauză de nouă luni, provocată de investigații privind propulsoarele laterale și motoarele BE-4, furnizate de Blue Origin, compania spațială a fondatorului Amazon, Jeff Bezos. Blue Origin participă la ancheta privind eșecul de duminică, potrivit unei surse Reuters. Deocamdată, nu există dovezi că motoarele BE-4 ar fi provocat defecțiunea. Misiunea era importantă și pentru Pentagon, care aștepta rezultatul zborului înainte de a autoriza reluarea lansărilor Vulcan cu încărcături de securitate națională. Pierderea celor 40 de sateliți complică planurile Amazon de a construi o rețea globală de internet prin satelit. Din 2025, compania a lansat 398 de sateliți Leo în cadrul a 14 misiuni, reprezentând aproximativ 12% din cei 3.236 necesari pentru acoperirea globală planificată. Amazon spera să înceapă furnizarea serviciilor de internet în 2026, însă întârzierile repetate ale partenerilor de lansare au îngreunat extinderea rețelei. Diferența față de Starlink rămâne considerabilă. Rețeaua SpaceX numără peste 11.000 de sateliți și deservește milioane de clienți din întreaga lume. Un avantaj major al SpaceX este că își lansează sateliții cu propriile rachete, în timp ce Amazon depinde de contractele cu operatori externi. Amazon a transmis că orice lansare presupune riscuri și că ULA rămâne un partener de încredere. Compania se așteaptă ca investigația să clarifice defecțiunea și să permită continuarea programului Vulcan. © G4Media.ro.

candidates.full: Якщо смартфон майже розрядився, а часу на підзарядку обмаль, пришвидшити процес допоможе одна вбудована функція. Йдеться про режим польоту – він вимикає бездротові модулі та знижує фонове навантаження на батарею, завдяки чому акумулятор швидше відновлює ємність. Як зазначає видання Interia Kobieta, у звичайному режимі модулі мобільного зв’язку та Wi-Fi безперервно споживають ресурси, навіть коли дисплей вимкнений. При активації авіарежиму телефон перестає витрачати заряд на підтримку з’єднання, і вся потужність від розетки надходить безпосередньо в акумулятор. Цей прийом особливо стане в пригоді, коли рівень заряду впав до критичних 3–4% і потрібно за 10–15 хвилин отримати максимум відсотків перед виходом з дому. Хоча швидка зарядка – не єдина причина частіше користуватися цією кнопкою. Коли ще стане пригоді режим польоту: - У місцях зі слабким сигналом. У дорозі, в горах або за містом смартфон витрачає багато енергії на безперервний пошук мережі. На це йде левова частка заряду. Авіарежим зупинить пошук мережі та збереже заряд батареї до повернення в зону стабільного прийому. - Під час закордонних поїздок. Щоб уникнути випадкових списань у роумінгу за фонові оновлення додатків та синхронізацію пошти, увімкніть режим польоту перед перетином кордону. При цьому Wi-Fi можна активувати окремо вже після увімкнення режиму польоту – так ви залишитеся на зв’язку в готелі без ризику витратити гроші з рахунку. - У разі збоїв мобільного інтернету. Якщо мережа "зависла" або не проходять дзвінки, не обов’язково перезавантажувати гаджет. Увімкніть режим польоту на 10–15 секунд і вимкніть його знову – модуль зв’язку перезапуститься та підключиться до найближчої стабільної вишки. - Для спокійного сну. Авіарежим на ніч позбавить від випадкових сповіщень і дзвінків, але залишить доступними будильник, камеру, нотатки та інші офлайн-функції смартфона. Режим польоту є на всіх сучасних моделях телефонів. Щоб увімкнути його на iPhone, проведіть пальцем вниз від правого верхнього кута екрана (або вгору від нижнього краю на старих моделях із кнопкою "Додому"), щоб відкрити Центр управління. Натисніть на іконку із зображенням літака, щоб вона стала помаранчевою – це миттєво вимкне всі бездротові з’єднання. На Android проведіть пальцем вниз від верхнього краю дисплея, щоб відкрити панель швидких налаштувань. Натисніть іконку "Режим польоту" (або "Авіарежим" у вигляді літака) – її колір зміниться, підтверджуючи активацію блокування мережі. Як бачите, авіарежим – це не просто обов'язкове налаштування в літаку, а корисний помічник у повсякденних ситуаціях. Раніше експерти пояснили, що означає значок плюса в колі на телефоні та як його вимкнути. УНІАН розповідав, як зрозуміти, чи прослуховує смартфон ваші розмови.

candidates.full: Cybersecurity Cybersecurity startup Corma raised $125 million in a Series A funding round led by New Enterprise Associates. The funding round boosts the market valuation of the year-old startup to $1 billion. Corma plans to use the new capital to scale its cyber-defense AI models and increase capacity to meet surging demand. This summary was generated with AI and reviewed by an editor. Read more about how we use artificial intelligence in our journalism. Cybersecurity startup Corma raised $125 million in a Series A funding round led by New Enterprise Associates. View more Cybersecurity startup Corma raised $125 million to build automated agents that run on cyber-trained artificial-intelligence models. Led by venture investor New Enterprise Associates, the Series A funding round comes three months after Corma emerged from stealth with $60 million in seed capital. NEA joins existing investors Sequoia Capital, Khosla Ventures and Coatue. The latest round boosts Corma’s market valuation to $1 billion, the company said. Corma, launched in 2025 and jointly based in Tel Aviv and San Francisco, develops autonomous AI agents powered by purpose-built foundation models trained for cyber defense. The goal is to counter hackers armed with agents trained with general AI models, such as those from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and other tech firms, which can identify cyber vulnerabilities at lightning speeds, said Corma’s co-founder and Chief Executive Alon Pluda. The same autonomous tools that are now writing the world’s software code are also learning to break it and launch attacks, Pluda said. Last month, cyber teams worldwide raced to patch AI-detected bugs in the underlying software of multiple tools used by businesses, government agencies and other organizations—an onslaught of threats dubbed “Black October.” “The scary part is when you plot the performance of these exact same models on offensive cybersecurity, finding vulnerabilities and exploiting them end-to-end, they are advancing exponentially,” Pluda said. Rather than training all-purpose AI models, Corma’s models are fed security audit logs and events, network flows, configurations and other cyber-related data. “We are training a domain-specific foundation model for defensive cybersecurity,” he said. The models are then used to develop a “workforce” of autonomous AI agents to support cyber teams to secure defenses. The new capital will go into scaling the models and ramping up capacity to meet surging demand, Pluda said. “The hardest challenge that we had to face recently is capacity.” Cybersecurity news, analysis and insights from WSJ's global team of reporters and editors. Corma joins a growing number of early-stage cyber startups drawing investor attention and outsize funding. Investing in global cyber startups, spanning seed to Series B funding rounds, hit a combined deal value of $4.7 billion through September, outpacing 2025’s full-year total of $3.8 billion, according to market research firm PitchBook. The gains come even as the overall number of deals has dropped to 248, down from 358 last year, PitchBook said. In September, Cylake, an AI-native cybersecurity startup, disclosed a $245 million capital injection through a convertible note, roughly six months after raising $45 million in a seed round. Armadin, an AI-powered cyber startup launched by Mandiant founder Kevin Mandia, in March announced a record-breaking $189.9 million in combined seed and Series A funding. Pluda said he doesn’t see these and other cyber startups as competitors, since Corma’s AI agents work within its enterprise customers’ existing security systems—using many of the tools these and other startups are developing. candidates.full: 👍 Новая модель войны На немецком полигоне Графенвер американские военные, с учетом опыта российско-украинского противостояния, провели демонстрацию того, как может выглядеть война нового поколения. Учение, получившее название «Автономная группа быстрого реагирования на случай чрезвычайных ситуаций» (R3ACT), проводилось при поддержке Инициативы сдерживания восточного фланга (EFDI) и оперативной структуры «Как армия сражается». ‼️ Целью учений было продемонстрировать, как группы дронов могут «пробить» ПВО противника и замедлить наступление сил. Так, в рамках маневров, ВС США провели групповую атаку из 18 дронов с использованием НРТК R3NEGADE. Показательно и то, что целью учений было именно подавление ПВО и замедление продвижения войск противника. Это уже не оборонительная логика защиты территории, а проработка первого этапа прорыва эшелонированной обороны. Иначе говоря, под риторикой технологического развития скрывается подготовка к сценарию, в котором рои автономных систем должны открывать путь для последующих действий основных сил. Официально всё это подаётся как развитие автономных технологий и повышение эффективности подразделений быстрого реагирования. Однако за техническими терминами просматривается совершенно иной смысл. В частности, Крымский мост был поражен с применением подобной тактики. 🔽 Тем самым, Запад обкатывает новую модель войны, где исход сражений будет определять не столько танки и самолёты, сколько способность запускать, координировать и массово применять автономные ударные системы быстрее противника. 🇧🇾 Belarus_VPO | chat | МАХ

candidates.full: Трамп заявил, что не слышал об ограничениях Starlink в Украине 4 - 16.11.2026, 19:41 - 1,180 Ранее о перебоях в работе терминалов сообщил Зеленский. Президент США Дональд Трамп не слышал об ограничениях доступа к спутниковым системам Starlink или Starshield в Украине. Об этом глава Белого дома заявил журналистам перед вылетом на Филиппины и в Китай для участия в мероприятиях по линии АСЕАН и АТЭС, сообщает Clash Report. Один из журналистов спросил американского президента, почему доступ к Starlink в Украине ограничен. «Я об этом не слышал», — ответил Трамп. Вопрос об ограничении работы спутниковой системы Starlink в Украине возник еще в октябре. В ночь на 14 октября украинская сторона сообщила о перебоях в работе терминалов: связь пропадала при движении аппаратов со скоростью более 160 км/ч. Позже украинские представители заявили об ужесточении ограничений.
